controls.label: Infrared color
controls.qualification: False color from its measured flux in three infrared bands (Sutlieff, Bonse et al. (2026), arXiv:2606.23801; zero points from the SVO Filter Profile Service). The disc itself is unresolved; darkening toward the edge from a model atmosphere.
controls.notes: Beta Pictoris d's brightness in three infrared bands as one color: red F444W 4.35 µm, green F410M 4.072 µm, blue ERIS L′ 3.78 µm (Sutlieff, Bonse et al. (2026), arXiv:2606.23801; zero points from the SVO Filter Profile Service), on a range shared with this planet alone, from zero to its brightest band (f444w), so the color shows its band ratios; brightness is not compared across planets at different distances. Not a natural color; nobody has resolved its disc. The darkening toward the edge is the quadratic law fitted to the JWST/NIRCam F410M intensity PICASO 4.1 (Batalha et al. 2019, ApJ 878, 70) computes from Exo-REM cloudy (Charnay et al. 2018, ApJ 854, 172; 3.16 times solar metallicity, C/O 0.65) model atmospheres at 600 K and log g 4, read between the models YGP_550K_logg3.5, YGP_550K_logg4.0, YGP_600K_logg3.5, YGP_600K_logg4.0 (u1 0.781, u2 0.156; the law fits each model's eight angles within 0.13% of the centre): a cloudy model, the one Sutlieff, Bonse et al. (2026), arXiv:2606.23801 fit to this planet, because no table reaches a planet this cold and nobody has resolved its disc.
